persons.name: Hiram Z. Britain
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Britain, Hiram Z. 2' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). persons.name: J. Garland
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED MAN ON A RECONSTRUCTED ROOF. The papers name him and this household's dwelling does not: what is attested is the person and his trade, and what remains the reconstruction's is everything about where he lived. He is printed as 'J. GARLAND' and the corpus reads his trade as cooper. Cited at the Democrat of 11 June 1834, column 11. THIS ROOF DID NOT COME FROM HIS RECORD. The household was raised by the occupation census because the town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings needed a cooper and no documented one was available; the register (data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json, action `replace_invented`) is what says one now is. The dwelling's existence, position and footprint are unchanged and still conjectural, and nothing here claims he slept in it — only that the town's need for this trade is met by a man the papers name rather than by one this project invented. The invented name this record used to carry, and its name_basis block, are retired: an invented name is not kept beside a documented one. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1); the placement is L205. He is placed nowhere in particular by his own record, which is the condition of taking ANY roof of his trade — a man the papers put on a named street takes only a roof the plat stands on that street (T-0367), and one they place somewhere this scene cannot honour is refused outright. READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - fourth of 4 cooper households in this layer, in the north division. A TOWN PACKING THOUSANDS OF HOGS A SEASON NEEDS COOPERS, AND THIS DATASET HELD NONE. Andreas records that Clybourne packed some 250 head of cattle and about 2,000 hogs in the season of 1833, that George W. Dole packed a further 250 cattle and 1,000 hogs at the same place, and that the Newberry & Dole house on the South Branch packed 300 cattle and 1,400 hogs in 1834 (scan p. 1151). Packed provisions travel in barrels and barrels are made by coopers. The documented layer holds a packer, two slaughter-houses and not one cooper. Four cooper households are inferred against the schedule's six W3 cooper, wagon or wheelwright shops. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one. RETIRED AN INVENTED NAME (T-0264). This household was raised by the occupation census and named from the invented-name pools. The newspaper register matched it to J. Garland, a documented cooper the corpus names 1 time(s) and places nowhere in particular, and he now holds the roof. What changed is WHO: the argument for the household, its dwelling and its position are untouched and still the reconstruction's, and the person's grade is `inferred` — a real man with reconstructed details — rather than `attested`, which would claim the dwelling too. tools/replace_invented_residents.py derives this deal and prints every candidate it refused. T-0489: reconstructed occupancy retired; evidence-based person retained and unplaced.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD — no trade recorded, in the south division, where it is counted after the re-family recorded above; it was drawn in the north division. NOBODY HERE IS NAMED BY ANY SOURCE. The 1840 Chicago schedule counts children under ten at 27% of the town and women of twenty to twenty-nine as its second-largest band; the 1835 layer the sources can name holds 15 women, because the rolls that name this town — a letter list, a voters' roll, a subscription — print men. That gap is the shape of the evidence and not a reading of the town, so the order book counts it bucket by bucket and this household is drawn against those counts. Every value on it carries the model row and the seed that redraws it, and a source naming a woman who kept her own house in this division retires the whole record. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). This household is one of the surplus the re-cut HOLDS rather than retires: the owner's ruling of 2026-09-24 re-families it into a cell the book still orders instead of un-writing it, and `refamilied` above is the whole of what that changed.

residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). The sources stop short of 1 July 1835 for this household and nothing puts it anywhere else; the town's rule (T-1386) counts it present, and no source says where it slept. The roof is the invention and the people are not.

persons.name: Medad I. Simmons
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Simmons, Medad I.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 22 October 1834, column 4 — dated 1834-10-22. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Simmons, Mrs. Mary E. | Profession. | April 5, 1858.” (second_presb_0310, printed page 171), admitted 1858-04-05 by profession. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Simmons' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins M. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” THE LINE IS A MARRIED WOMAN'S ENTRY, and the crosswalk's own Mrs rule governs what it can have met: “a line flagged a_married_womans_entry that meets a MAN in the 1835 layer has met his name, not him: it corroborates that the name was a Chicago name in the 1840s and it does not put that man on this roll.” The match is filed rather than suppressed, because a suppressed match is invisible and a flagged one can be argued with. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive.
